steps.name: April
steps.text: Phew, that mission got me all sweaty.

steps.name: April
steps.text: I'd better hurry home and shower.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Oh, who's that over there...?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: Alright, that's the letter and every last cent accounted for.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Thanks a lot.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: Hah, don't worry about it. You're a very good customer. Pretty much your whole family knows me by now.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: But you haven't been back in a while, huh? Why not take a trip home? Your uncle's gonna ask me to drag you back to Rim Billiton as soon as he sees me.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: Not that I'm one to talk, the way I've been running around for a year and change. But you know all the letters in the world can't compare with you going home in person.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: ...I know. It's just, there's still patients here who need me.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: When I have some free time, I'll go back.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: Well, I think you've got a handle on it, so I'll leave it here for now.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: Anyway, I'll check over the letters again and then head out.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: Need any goodies? Or just the usual?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Yes, get a box of those peppermint candies from the shop below my home.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Sorry, Uncle...

steps.name: April
steps.text: So they've got Messengers at Rhodes Island too.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Have we been introduced...?

steps.name: April
steps.text: I'm new here, codename's April. But you can call me April.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Nice to meet you, April. I'm Ansel, from Medical.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: There are lots of Messenger at Rhodes Island. And Messengers like the one just now aren't our operators, they're Messengers who exclusively serve us Rhodes Islanders.

steps.name: April
steps.text: What's the difference?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: We have some Messengers who do become operators. Oh, like Angelina. Do you know her?

steps.name: April
steps.text: Yeah. She's a Messenger girl, about my age?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Right. A lot of Messengers get sick and end up working for us as operators to offset the cost of treatment. That's what happened with Angelina.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Oh, me too.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Yes. So you know the cost of Oripathy treatment is by no means low. There are all kinds of people from all walks of life here on the ship for more or less the same reason.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Isn't that pretty much the same as becoming a Messenger here though?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Ahaha. I guess it is kind of confusing, but no.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Because Messenger work doesn't involve much contact with other people, and you're always traveling all around, you can still do it even after becoming Infected.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Basically, most people aren't going to know if the person bringing them their mail is Infected or not...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: The point is they can keep doing their work same as they always were, as long as they come to Rhodes Island for regular treatment.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Huh. So they can just like, do their own thing?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Exactly. We usually give operators like that some long-term field work missions.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: And they tend to use Rhodes Island as a waystation for their work. And if they happen to be going near some friends or relatives of our operators, we'll usually ask them to bring a letter or something.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: But for someone like me, who writes home regularly, I need something more predictable.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: With very few Messengers from Rim Billiton at Rhodes Island right now.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Whew, it all feels so loose... I couldn't imagine anything like that at my old company.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Anything like what?

steps.name: April
steps.text: The employees having so much freedom! There must be some folks who come by once and never come back, right?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: You're a sharp one. That does happen sometimes, and we do follow up on it. But no matter what happens, you can't leave a patient unattended.

steps.name: April
steps.text: You're a real good person, Dr. Ansel.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Thanks. I'm just here to help people.

steps.name: April
steps.text: But that means Rhodes Island definitely needs some dedicated Messengers.

steps.name: April
steps.text: I never thought about this stuff before.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Say, April, you're from Rim Billiton too, aren't you?

steps.name: April
steps.text: Yep. I'm from the south side of Iron Carrot City.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Oh, I know that place. Your hometown always tops the annual charts in ore production.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Yeah, that's home. We're supposed to be really proud of that productivity, but I can't say it does much for me.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I'm from Iron Fist City. Do you have any relatives back home you need to contact?

steps.name: April
steps.text: Nope.

steps.name: April
steps.text: My parents died in a mine accident when I was little. The company raised me.

steps.name: April
steps.text: When I grew up, I worked for them as a hunter. It didn't pay great, but I got by, until I caught Oripathy...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: ...I'm sorry.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Nah, it's fine.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I've heard that Rim Billiton's companies actually treat the Infected pretty decently?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Because of how important the mining industry is, people back home end up coming into contact with Oripathy a lot more than in other countries...

steps.name: April
steps.text: That's what I thought at first, but after living through it, I was so, so wrong.

steps.name: April
steps.text: They like to talk about all the benefits they offer, but down in the fine print they have all kinds of deductibles and copays. And once they know you've got Oripathy, you'll suddenly find all your work drying up.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Oripathy sufferers on their own, like me, just can't survive.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Oh... I had no idea.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: No wonder so many of my old workmates who caught Oripathy just disappeared...

steps.name: April
steps.text: Anyway, I lost my company ID and the lease on my room, so there's nothing for me back in Rim Billiton anymore.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Hey now, don't you give me that look, Dr. Ansel. I can't stand pity.

steps.name: April
steps.text: I made it to Rhodes Island, didn't I?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I guess you did.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Anyways, I thought you looked kinda sad when you were sending that letter. Did something happen?

steps.name: April
steps.text: Oh, but you don't have to tell me if it's something really personal. And I won't tell anyone either!

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: April, did you have lunch yet?

steps.name: April
steps.text: No, I just got back from a mission. I was about to go take a shower.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Let me buy you lunch. This is a pretty long story.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Huh? Okay.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Wow, Dr. Ansel, you sure eat healthy.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: It comes with the job, I guess. And you can drop the 'doctor', just Ansel is fine. We're pretty much the same age, right?

steps.name: April
steps.text: Okay~

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Eat up, first. We'll get into it after we've taken the edge off.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: ...I always say I wish I could see my family, but the truth is I don't really want to go back.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: There's some stuff I don't want to deal with.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I have three older brothers and one baby sister, but my parents are long gone. Mom, to lung disease. Dad, overwork.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: But I had it better than you. By the time they went, my brothers were old enough to work.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I was the only one still too young. So when he died, my dad had me sent to live with my uncle, his older brother. My sister went to his younger brother.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Yeah, that happens a lot. If I had any relatives, I'd have ended up like that.

steps.name: April
steps.text: My dad once told me all our relatives went to other cities.

steps.name: April
steps.text: So you don't wanna go back because your uncle was bad to you?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: No. My uncle was a manager at a small company. He was serious and strict, but he treated me well, really just like his own son.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: It's just...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: He didn't want me to become a doctor.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: When I was little, I helped out at Uncle's company. He was grooming me to take over his job.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I didn't listen to him. I decided to become a doctor, and went far away to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Woah. So you're a runaway, Ansel?!

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Ahaha, no, I wouldn't go that far.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: There was some time between my decision to study medicine and me actually coming to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I talked it over with Uncle many times. Sometimes our conversations got pretty heated.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: But in the end, he respected my choice, and agreed I could become a doctor.

steps.name: April
steps.text: I get where he's coming from. I never got the impression it was easy to practice medicine in Rim Billiton.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Right. First, it's tough to get started. Then, it's tough to keep going.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: A lot of mine doctors only have the most basic medical training.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: It definitely wouldn't be as stable a life as working for Uncle's company, and it'd be hard to find a job.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I seriously considered going with his plan. It really isn't a bad place to work.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: And he did so much for me. I felt like I couldn't let him down.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Sure, that makes sense. But everyone has a dream.

steps.name: April
steps.text: It sounds like your uncle is a real good bloke, though. If my mom and dad were still around, I don't think they'd be okay with something like that.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Right. And in the end, I followed through on my decision.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: But Uncle isn't the type to keep his feelings bottled up inside. He's been with the company for half his life, and he still hopes I'll go back to continue his work someday.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I've been back twice, and it's always hard.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: And my brothers are even more opposed to what I do. But I send them money, so they keep their mouths shut.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: My sister, on the other hand, is pretty supportive.

steps.name: April
steps.text: I can't really relate to any of that.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Let's just say everybody's got baggage.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I think I'm doing the right thing. And Rhodes Island treats me well.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: But... it is what it is.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: There's nothing I can do to change how Uncle feels.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I can only work harder and do better for myself, and my own goals.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: And one day I'll be able to go back, puff out my chest and say: 'Look, Uncle, see how many people I've saved? I made a huge contribution to the fight against Oripathy.'

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: ...But I guess by then I'll probably be brave enough to just face him anyway.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Soft and weak as you look, Ansel, who would've thought you've got all this going on?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I can't tell if that's supposed to be a compliment.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Of course it is.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Hah, alright, then.

steps.name: April
steps.text: But it sounds like you actually do want to go back home?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: ...I guess I do.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Going around the world with Rhodes Island is a great way to broaden your horizons, but no matter what happens, Rim Billiton is still my home.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I miss the giant smoke stacks, the din of machinery, the miners and their work chants, the noisy streets...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Maybe someday I'll leave Rhodes and head back home to practice medicine.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: April
steps.text: Nothing. I was just thinking about how even though I say I don't miss Rim Billiton at all, I don't know if maybe I would go back.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Ansel, do you know where my codename comes from?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: April is like, a month? Fourth one on the calendar?

steps.name: April
steps.text: Yes, but also no. It's the name of a song about spring.

steps.name: April
steps.text: I never felt like I liked Rim Billiton. I don't like any of the stuff you've been talking about.

steps.name: April
steps.text: My memories of home are all dark and dusty, I feel like I can barely breathe when I remember them.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Life wasn't easy even before I got Oripathy.

steps.name: April
steps.text: I had to show up to the office every day, and then go out with the team whenever they had a job.

steps.name: April
steps.text: I made some money, but it was real hard out there. A ten day trip was common, and sometimes we'd even be gone for a month or two.

steps.name: April
steps.text: And it's not like there was much to do when we didn't have a job either.

steps.name: April
steps.text: The bands I liked were in other countries and cosmetics would only show up in magazines.

steps.name: April
steps.text: With all the factories polluting the air, I had to put so much into my skin care routine.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Those factories, and even just the streets were so noisy they'd wake me up in the middle of the night.

steps.name: April
steps.text: And would you believe my apartment was so lousy I'd run out of water right in the middle of a shower sometimes?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Phew, those don't sound like good memories...

steps.name: April
steps.text: But, when I really think about it, there were good times too.

steps.name: April
steps.text: It was a ruthless, cutthroat company for sure, but they took care of me for years. I don't know what the upper management was like, but I remember when I went to the office to talk about my benefits, the people there definitely weren't happy about what they had to do.

steps.name: April
steps.text: My neighbors had their issues, but they still helped me. Old Man Perot upstairs was always so mean to everyone, but he started giving me food after he found out I was sick.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Oh, but Old Mrs. Lolo downstairs was the worst. She spat whenever she saw me.

steps.name: April
steps.text: The supermarket down there had all kinds of good stuff on rotation too. Speaking of, I don't think I've ever seen meatballs like that anywhere else. Those were super tasty.

steps.name: April
steps.text: And of course, the time I spent with mom and dad when I was little was real happy.

steps.name: April
steps.text: I know what's going on here, I'm just getting a strong hit of nostalgia.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Hahaha, maybe.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: But still, I think we can never really abandon our roots.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: When I came to Rhodes Island, I learned how vast our world is, and all the wonderful ways one can live a life.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I've thought about trying another life for myself, like becoming a Vanguard Operator or a caster. Or going into civilian work.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: And I could just choose a new life for myself. No one would stop me.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: But in the end, I decided to keep on practicing medicine.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I was born in Rim Billiton, and I grew up among the workers. Unless I suddenly woke up with amnesia someday, there's no way I could deny my past.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Speaking of amnesia, did I hear that the Doctor has it?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Oh, yes. That's no secret.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Going with what you said earlier, do you think the Doctor could choose a new life?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: ...I think that would be pretty hard.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I don't know the Doctor's past, but Amiya, Dr. Kal'tsit, and lots of others do.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I think a lot of the things the Doctor does are not exactly done by choice.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: So I guess that means even if you do lose your memory, you're still stuck with your past.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Yeah. How did we get here from talking about hometowns?

steps.name: April
steps.text: Anyway, your hometown is definitely the most important part of your past.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Right. But it's not really the town itself that matters, it's the mark left on you by the time you spent there.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I could've given up that mark, but I decided to hold onto it.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: April
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: April
steps.text: I dunno. I never thought about it before.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Doesn't matter. We're still young. We've got a lot of time to figure that one out.

steps.name: April
steps.text: But I guess I didn't leave Rim Billiton to get away from that life, at least.

steps.name: April
steps.text: If I could've kept on living there, I probably would've. I just didn't have a choice.

steps.name: April
steps.text: I suffered a lot after I became Infected, yeah, but I can't keep on hating people, and saying stuff like I hate Rim Billiton.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: That's totally normal. When someone gets Infected, his whole worldview doesn't turn on a dime.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: You'll have a better understanding after you live at Rhodes Island for a while. At least for now, we can keep talking about home, and our past.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Right, well, I guess I have to admit I'm the accepting type, huh?

steps.name: April
steps.text: I probably won't say I like Rim Billiton, but I can say I like Iron Carrot City.

steps.name: April
steps.text: I'll never forget how, whenever I was feeling down, I'd head up to the roof of my apartment building.

steps.name: April
steps.text: It wasn't that tall. There were other, taller ones around.

steps.name: April
steps.text: And I'd feel fenced in, trapped by those tall buildings around me. Like the piece of sky straight up above me was all I could see.

steps.name: April
steps.text: But it was also kind of reassuring, because I don't need a lot of space. I don't like having too many choices. A little coziness is just right for me.

steps.name: April
steps.text: I'd look around and see what the neighbors were doing. Sometimes I'd see something fun, sometimes I wouldn't. But it didn't matter.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Then I'd lie down in the middle of the rooftop, put on my headphones, and play my favorite song: 'April.' I'd think about whatever, and take a nice nap.

steps.name: April
steps.text: By the time I woke up, most of my worries would be gone.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Sounds great.

steps.name: April
steps.text: It was. I wish I could find a place like that here, but the Rhodes Island deck is just too wide and open for me.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: I'll point you towards an operator named Kroos. She's got a lot of experience finding places to slack off.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Really? That'd be great! I'll go find her in a bit!

steps.name: April
steps.text: But after all that, I do kinda feel like I want to go back home.

steps.name: April
steps.text: It's your fault.

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Hah, well, I'm sorry.

steps.name: April
steps.text: I'll set that aside for now. I'm still new here. I can't go taking a vacation right away.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Oh, I know!

steps.name: April
steps.text: Is that Messenger you hired to send your letter gone yet?

steps.name: Ansel
steps.text: Probably not. I think he's here until tomorrow.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Great, I'll go get him!

steps.name: April
steps.text: Mr. Messenger! You're going to Rim Billiton, right?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: Sure am, little Cautus. Do you want to send something?

steps.name: April
steps.text: April's fine. But it's not a letter, I was hoping you could do something for me?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: What?

steps.name: April
steps.text: When you're in Rim Billiton, could you please go to the top of a tall building and take a picture of the view up there?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: Huh? Kind of a weird request.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Messenger
steps.text: ...But it doesn't sound hard. I could probably do that.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Oh, thank you so much!

steps.name: April
steps.text: My hometown, my past... turns out I care more than I thought I did.

steps.name: April
steps.text: Well, anyway, what really matters now is meeting that Kroos girl. Finding a nice place to nap is a much more realistic goal than going home!
